31: ## 2. OVERVIEW
32: 
33: ### What It Does
34: 
35: cli-opencode is the single routing point for runtimes that need an OpenCode dispatch. A smart router scores the prompt against intent signals (external dispatch, parallel detached, cross-AI handback, agent delegation, cross-repo) and loads only the references that match. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version: on OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) the default dispatch is `cd <repo-root> && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json "<prompt>"`. On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated, it is `opencode run --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir <repo-root>`. A three-layer guard refuses self-invocation unless the request is an explicit parallel detached session.
36: 
37: It does not write application code or manage spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns spec folders, memory and continuity. cli-opencode dispatches to OpenCode and hands the result back to the caller.
38: 
39: ### Why This Skill Exists
40: 
41: An external session that needs the project's whole runtime has no native path to get it. Every plugin and skill, the registered MCP servers, the spec folders and their continuity docs: none of that loads from outside. Hand-building an `opencode run` invocation hits the non-obvious traps. The dispatch hangs at zero percent CPU when stdin stays open. The current OpenCode rejects a top-level `--agent general` without saying why. A caller that is itself OpenCode risks a self-dispatch loop that burns tokens. This skill standardizes the dispatch across the documented use cases and refuses self-invocation.
42: 
43: ### The Dispatch Surface
44: 
45: | Capability | What the skill can operate |
46: |---|---|
47: | **One-shot full-runtime dispatch** | `opencode run` loads every plugin in `opencode.json`, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every MCP server registered there |
48: | **Parallel detached sessions** | separate session ids and state in the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/` database for ablation suites and worker farms |
49: | **Cross-AI handback** | bridges the dispatch result back into the caller's spec folder through the Memory Handback |
50: | **Provider and model surface** | reaches every configured provider catalog through `references/providers-and-models.md`, which is the roster |
51: | **Agent delegation** | routes to project-local agents under `.skilled/agents/` with the primary-versus-subagent caveats in `references/agent-delegation.md` |
52: 
53: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. 63: ```

69: ```bash

71: ```

73: Expected when configured: a table of providers with status and default indicators. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions), the skill asks before falling back rather than substituting a model you did not approve.

79: cd "$REPO_ROOT" && opencode run --standalone \
80:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \

117: 
118: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
119: 
120: ### The Dispatch Lifecycle
121: 
122: The calling AI composes a prompt, passes it through the smart router to load matching references, then dispatches `opencode run` with an explicit model, variant, format and directory. OpenCode starts a session that loads every plugin in `opencode.json`, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every MCP server registered there. The calling AI parses the JSON event stream incrementally, validates the output and integrates it. The whole round-trip is non-interactive: send the prompt, get the response, exit.
123: 
124: ### The Full-Runtime Difference
125: 
126: This is what sets cli-opencode apart from every sibling in the cli-* family. A sibling dispatch sends a raw model behind a thin CLI wrapper, with no plugins, no skills and no MCP tools. `opencode run` loads the project wholesale. One command gives the dispatched session the skill advisor, Code Mode's external-service manuals, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every project-specific plugin. That is the reason you reach for this skill when the task needs project context rather than a model alone.
127: 
128: ### The Two Non-Obvious Rules
129: 
130: Two `opencode run` defaults punish operators who learn them the hard way.
131: 
132: **Rule 1: use `--agent` deliberately.** The live dispatch contract does not support direct top-level routing to `context`, `review`, `debug` or the other subagents the roster names. None of them is directly invokable as a top-level `opencode run --agent` route. Do not pass `--agent general`. The default path is selected by omitting `--agent`. Some small-model paths documented in `SKILL.md` carry narrower omit-agent caveats.
133: 
134: **Rule 2: append `</dev/null` to every non-interactive run.** Without closed stdin, `opencode run` hangs at zero percent CPU after the snapshot-cleanup line. A foreground `| tail` bypasses this because the upstream pipe stage provides closed stdin, but `> stdout.log 2> stderr.log` does not. Position `</dev/null` after the prompt argument, before the redirects.
135: 
136: ### The Self-Invocation Guard
137: 
138: If the agent reading this skill is already inside OpenCode, the skill refuses to load. The guard checks three layers in order:
139: 
140: 1. The `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` env var and any `OPENCODE_*`-prefixed vars, which OpenCode sets on session start.
141: 2. Process ancestry, where an `opencode` parent in the tree trips the guard.
142: 3. A best-effort lock-file probe under `~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock`, a heuristic layer since that path does not exist on every install.
143: 
144: The one exception is an explicit parallel detached request. When the prompt contains "parallel detached", "ablation suite", "worker farm" or "spawn detached", the guard allows the dispatch because it spawns a separate session id, not a self-dispatch.
145: 
146: ### Provider Auth Pre-Flight
147: 
148: Before the first dispatch in a session the skill checks each provider on OpenCode 2 by filtering `opencode models --standalone` for the `<provider-id>/` prefix, or, on OpenCode 1 (fallback), with `opencode models <provider-id>`. The providers, their models and their effort ceilings live in `references/providers-and-models.md`, which is the roster. Restating them here is how the two copies come to disagree. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions) the skill asks before falling back and never substitutes a model you did not approve. The full roster and effort map live in `references/providers-and-models.md`.
149: 
150: ### Agent Delegation
151: 
152: OpenCode resolves project-local agent files from `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`, but the live dispatch contract is narrower than file presence alone. Subagents such as `context`, `review`, `debug` and the rest of the roster are invoked through a primary path, never as direct specialist `opencode run --agent` slugs. Use `orchestrate` for generic subagent routing when help-verified, omit `--agent` for the default path and never pass `--agent general`. Some small-model paths documented in `SKILL.md` carry narrower omit-agent caveats. The full roster lives in `references/agent-delegation.md`.
153:

A non-Anthropic CLI that needs OpenCode as a bridge to a project subsystem such as spec-kit or the skill advisor also lands here. Skip it for simple tasks the caller can answer directly, for raw model dispatch where a sibling cli-* is leaner, for the interactive OpenCode TUI and for anything a plain shell command already covers.

246: ## 7. TROUBLESHOOTING
247: 
248: | What you see | Why | Fix |
249: |---|---|---|
250: | `command not found: opencode` | CLI not installed or PATH not updated | `brew install opencode` or `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install \| bash`, then restart your terminal |
251: | Dispatch hangs at 0% CPU after the snapshot line | Missing `</dev/null` on a non-interactive run | Append `</dev/null` before any `> stdout.log 2> stderr.log` redirect |
252: | `--agent general` fails or warns | The default path is selected by omitting `--agent` | Omit `--agent general`. Use `orchestrate` only when it is the documented primary route and help-verified. Route `context`, `review`, `debug` and `ai-council` through the documented primary path (or, for `ai-council`, `/deep:ai-council`) instead of a direct top-level `--agent`. |
253: | `provider/model not found` or `401 Unauthorized` | The default provider is not configured on this machine (`llmgateway` on both versions) | Run `opencode providers list` (OpenCode 1) or `opencode models --standalone` (OpenCode 2), then log in the missing provider |
254: | Empty event stream | Output format defaulted to formatted instead of JSON | Force `--format json` |
255: | `Self-invocation refused` | The caller is already inside OpenCode (`OPENCODE_*` env, `opencode` ancestry or a state lock) | Use a different runtime, exit the current session or restate with explicit parallel-detached keywords |
256: | Unknown `--variant` flag on OpenCode 1 | Binary older than the documented baseline | Run `opencode --version` and `opencode run --help`, then upgrade. It has no `run` form on OpenCode 2. See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md) |
257: | Context too large or truncated | The prompt references broad paths instead of specific files | Split large tasks and use `--file` for attachments |

260: 
261: ## 8. FAQ
262: 
263: **Q: What does the full-runtime dispatch buy over a sibling cli-* skill?**
264: 
265: A: A sibling cli-* skill dispatches to a single provider's binary. cli-opencode dispatches into a session that loads every plugin, skill and registered MCP server for the project. When the task needs a project-local skill, a project-specific plugin or the skill advisor, only cli-opencode provides all of them in one shot. When it only needs a model, a sibling is leaner.
266: 
267: **Q: When do I need a parallel detached session?**
268: 
269: A: When you are inside OpenCode and want a second session with its own state and session id. Common patterns are an ablation suite across sessions, a worker farm for parallel research and a cross-repo research branch. On OpenCode 2, `--port` has no `run` form (OpenCode 1 only). See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md). The prompt must contain explicit parallel-session keywords or the self-invocation guard blocks the dispatch.
270: 
271: **Q: Why no top-level `--agent`?**
272: 
273: A: OpenCode 2 accepts `--agent general`. OpenCode 1 (fallback) treats named agents like `general` as subagents and will not run them at the top level: it prints a warning, falls back to the default agent and exits 0, so the flag does not select the requested agent. The default agent already covers the general case. For a specific profile, describe the role in the prompt body.
274: 
275: **Q: Why does a non-interactive dispatch hang without `</dev/null`?**
276: 
277: A: OpenCode reads stdin at startup before session creation. When stdout and stderr are redirected to files, stdin stays open and the process waits forever. Appending `</dev/null` provides an immediate EOF so the dispatch continues.
278: 
279: **Q: Which model do I pick?**
280: 
281: A: Default to `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` on both versions. On OpenCode 2 (the expected version) the default is `-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`, through the same gateway, because v2 lists no `opencode-go` provider unless it is logged in separately. On OpenCode 1 (fallback) that is `--model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max`, through the DevPass LLM Gateway, which fronts the latency-optimized reasoning model at its max thinking tier. The `opencode-go` Go-plan quota is spent, so that route hangs on "Go usage limit exceeded". One provider now serves both versions. Switch to `minimax/MiniMax-M3` for MiniMax Direct or `openai/gpt-6-sol` for paid premium. The full roster lives in `references/providers-and-models.md`.
282:

284:

287: The skill ships a manual testing playbook with per-feature scenarios grouped by category: CLI invocation, external dispatch, multi-provider routing, agent routing, session continuity, integration patterns, prompt templates, parallel detached sessions and cross-repo or cross-server dispatch.

31: ## 2. OVERVIEW
32: 
33: ### What It Does
34: 
35: cli-opencode is the single routing point for runtimes that need an OpenCode dispatch. A smart router scores the prompt against intent signals (external dispatch, parallel detached, cross-AI handback, agent delegation, cross-repo) and loads only the references that match. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version: on OpenCode 2 (2.0.32) the default dispatch is `cd <repo-root> && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json "<prompt>"`. On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated, it is `opencode run --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir <repo-root>`. A three-layer guard refuses self-invocation unless the request is an explicit parallel detached session.
36: 
37: It does not write application code or manage spec folders. `sk-code` owns code standards and tests. `system-spec-kit` owns spec folders, memory and continuity. cli-opencode dispatches to OpenCode and hands the result back to the caller.
38: 
39: ### Why This Skill Exists
40: 
41: An external session that needs the project's whole runtime has no native path to get it. Every plugin and skill, the registered MCP servers, the spec folders and their continuity docs: none of that loads from outside. Hand-building an `opencode run` invocation hits the non-obvious traps. The dispatch hangs at zero percent CPU when stdin stays open. The current OpenCode rejects a top-level `--agent general` without saying why. A caller that is itself OpenCode risks a self-dispatch loop that burns tokens. This skill standardizes the dispatch across the documented use cases and refuses self-invocation.
42: 
43: ### The Dispatch Surface
44: 
45: | Capability | What the skill can operate |
46: |---|---|
47: | **One-shot full-runtime dispatch** | `opencode run` loads every plugin in `opencode.json`, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every MCP server registered there |
48: | **Parallel detached sessions** | separate session ids and state in the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/` database for ablation suites and worker farms |
49: | **Cross-AI handback** | bridges the dispatch result back into the caller's spec folder through the Memory Handback |
50: | **Provider and model surface** | reaches every configured provider catalog through `references/providers-and-models.md`, which is the roster |
51: | **Agent delegation** | routes to project-local agents under `.skilled/agents/` with the primary-versus-subagent caveats in `references/agent-delegation.md` |
52: 
53: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. Flag and provider observations that name 2.0.32 or 1.19.3 were read on those releases and have not been re-read on 2.1.4 or 1.19.4. OpenCode 2 is the expected and recommended version. OpenCode 1 is supported for now as a fallback for users who have not updated. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md).

57: ## 3. QUICK START
58: 
59: **Step 1: Verify the CLI is installed.**
60: 
61: ```bash
62: command -v opencode2 || command -v opencode
63: ```
64: 
65: If nothing prints, install with `brew install opencode` (macOS) or `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`. On the recommended layout `opencode` is OpenCode 2 and `opencode1` is the OpenCode 1 fallback. A machine with only OpenCode 1 answers to `opencode`.
66: 
67: **Step 2: Run the provider auth pre-flight.**
68: 
69: ```bash
70: opencode providers list
71: ```
72: 
73: Expected when configured: a table of providers with status and default indicators. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions), the skill asks before falling back rather than substituting a model you did not approve.
74: 
75: **Step 3: Run the default dispatch.**
76: 
77: ```bash
78: # On OpenCode 2 (2.0.32), the expected version:
79: cd "$REPO_ROOT" && opencode run --standalone \
80:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
81:   --format json \
82:   "Act as a context-retrieval agent: search the spec docs with the ripgrep retrieval conventions and return the top findings." \
83:   </dev/null
84: ```
85: 
86: ```bash
87: # On OpenCode 1 (1.19.3), supported for now as a fallback:
88: opencode run \
89:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max \
90:   --format json \
91:   --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
92:   "Act as a context-retrieval agent: search the spec docs with the ripgrep retrieval conventions and return the top findings." \
93:   </dev/null
94: ```
95: 
96: The two versions do not always list the same providers, so on OpenCode 2 check that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m` first. OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider on this machine, and the `opencode-go` Go-plan quota is spent on OpenCode 1, so `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is the single default on both versions.
97: 
98: You get structured JSON events streamed to stdout as the session runs: `step_start`, `tool_use`, `text` and `step_finish`, every one carrying a `sessionID`, with the reply text in `text` events. The `</dev/null` is mandatory on non-interactive runs on both versions, because the hang is observed on OpenCode 1 and unverified on OpenCode 2. Do not pass top-level `--agent` by default: `context`, `review`, `debug` and `ai-council` are subagents that route through a primary path (or, for `ai-council`, through its own `/deep:ai-council` command). Top-level `--agent` is only conditionally allowed for primary agents such as `plan` or `orchestrate` after `opencode run --help` confirms acceptance. When a specific agent profile matters, describe it in the prompt body instead, as this example does.

102: > **Do not pass `--share`.** OpenCode 2 `run` has no such flag. On OpenCode 1.19.3 (fallback) it is a hidden, deprecated flag that prints "Session sharing has been discontinued" and publishes nothing.

106: opencode run --port 4096 \
107:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir "$REPO_ROOT" \
108:   "Run a parallel research branch for the approved spec folder." \
109:   </dev/null &
110: ```

112: On OpenCode 2, `--port` has no `run` form (OpenCode 1 only). See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md).
113: 
114: The session runs under its own session id in the shared `~/.local/share/opencode/` database (`opencode.db`, `storage/`, `snapshot/`), inspectable independently via `opencode export <sessionID>`. On OpenCode 2 there is no share URL because `run` has no share flag, and on OpenCode 1.19.3 `--share` is a deprecated no-op that publishes nothing.

116: ---
117: 
118: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
119: 
120: ### The Dispatch Lifecycle
121: 
122: The calling AI composes a prompt, passes it through the smart router to load matching references, then dispatches `opencode run` with an explicit model, variant, format and directory. OpenCode starts a session that loads every plugin in `opencode.json`, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every MCP server registered there. The calling AI parses the JSON event stream incrementally, validates the output and integrates it. The whole round-trip is non-interactive: send the prompt, get the response, exit.
123: 
124: ### The Full-Runtime Difference
125: 
126: This is what sets cli-opencode apart from every sibling in the cli-* family. A sibling dispatch sends a raw model behind a thin CLI wrapper, with no plugins, no skills and no MCP tools. `opencode run` loads the project wholesale. One command gives the dispatched session the skill advisor, Code Mode's external-service manuals, every skill under `.opencode/skills/` and every project-specific plugin. That is the reason you reach for this skill when the task needs project context rather than a model alone.
127: 
128: ### The Two Non-Obvious Rules
129: 
130: Two `opencode run` defaults punish operators who learn them the hard way.
131: 
132: **Rule 1: use `--agent` deliberately.** The live dispatch contract does not support direct top-level routing to `context`, `review`, `debug` or the other subagents the roster names. None of them is directly invokable as a top-level `opencode run --agent` route. Do not pass `--agent general`. The default path is selected by omitting `--agent`. Some small-model paths documented in `SKILL.md` carry narrower omit-agent caveats.
133: 
134: **Rule 2: append `</dev/null` to every non-interactive run.** Without closed stdin, `opencode run` hangs at zero percent CPU after the snapshot-cleanup line. A foreground `| tail` bypasses this because the upstream pipe stage provides closed stdin, but `> stdout.log 2> stderr.log` does not. Position `</dev/null` after the prompt argument, before the redirects.
135: 
136: ### The Self-Invocation Guard
137: 
138: If the agent reading this skill is already inside OpenCode, the skill refuses to load. The guard checks three layers in order:
139: 
140: 1. The `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` env var and any `OPENCODE_*`-prefixed vars, which OpenCode sets on session start.
141: 2. Process ancestry, where an `opencode` parent in the tree trips the guard.
142: 3. A best-effort lock-file probe under `~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock`, a heuristic layer since that path does not exist on every install.
143: 
144: The one exception is an explicit parallel detached request. When the prompt contains "parallel detached", "ablation suite", "worker farm" or "spawn detached", the guard allows the dispatch because it spawns a separate session id, not a self-dispatch.
145: 
146: ### Provider Auth Pre-Flight
147: 
148: Before the first dispatch in a session the skill checks each provider on OpenCode 2 by filtering `opencode models --standalone` for the `<provider-id>/` prefix, or, on OpenCode 1 (fallback), with `opencode models <provider-id>`. The providers, their models and their effort ceilings live in `references/providers-and-models.md`, which is the roster. Restating them here is how the two copies come to disagree. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions) the skill asks before falling back and never substitutes a model you did not approve. The full roster and effort map live in `references/providers-and-models.md`.
149: 
150: ### Agent Delegation
151: 
152: OpenCode resolves project-local agent files from `.opencode/agents/<slug>.md`, but the live dispatch contract is narrower than file presence alone. Subagents such as `context`, `review`, `debug` and the rest of the roster are invoked through a primary path, never as direct specialist `opencode run --agent` slugs. Use `orchestrate` for generic subagent routing when help-verified, omit `--agent` for the default path and never pass `--agent general`. Some small-model paths documented in `SKILL.md` carry narrower omit-agent caveats. The full roster lives in `references/agent-delegation.md`.
153: 
154: ---

215: ## 6. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION
216: 
217: ### When To Use This Skill
218: 
219: Reach for cli-opencode when a task needs the project's full runtime: every plugin, skill and MCP tool. Use it too for a parallel detached session on ablation or worker-farm work. A non-Anthropic CLI that needs OpenCode as a bridge to a project subsystem such as spec-kit or the skill advisor also lands here. Skip it for simple tasks the caller can answer directly, for raw model dispatch where a sibling cli-* is leaner, for the interactive OpenCode TUI and for anything a plain shell command already covers.
220: 
221: ### Sibling Boundaries
222: 
223: The cli-X skills each dispatch to a different provider and never overlap.
224:

226: |---|---|---|
227: | `cli-opencode` | OpenCode | Full project runtime, parallel detached sessions, cross-AI handback |
228: | `cli-claude-code` | Anthropic | Deep reasoning, diff-based edits, `--json-schema` output, agent delegation |
229: | `cli-codex` | OpenAI | Sandboxed coding, repo analysis, PR review, web research |

246: ## 7. TROUBLESHOOTING
247: 
248: | What you see | Why | Fix |
249: |---|---|---|
250: | `command not found: opencode` | CLI not installed or PATH not updated | `brew install opencode` or `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install \| bash`, then restart your terminal |
251: | Dispatch hangs at 0% CPU after the snapshot line | Missing `</dev/null` on a non-interactive run | Append `</dev/null` before any `> stdout.log 2> stderr.log` redirect |
252: | `--agent general` fails or warns | The default path is selected by omitting `--agent` | Omit `--agent general`. Use `orchestrate` only when it is the documented primary route and help-verified. Route `context`, `review`, `debug` and `ai-council` through the documented primary path (or, for `ai-council`, `/deep:ai-council`) instead of a direct top-level `--agent`. |
253: | `provider/model not found` or `401 Unauthorized` | The default provider is not configured on this machine (`llmgateway` on both versions) | Run `opencode providers list` (OpenCode 1) or `opencode models --standalone` (OpenCode 2), then log in the missing provider |
254: | Empty event stream | Output format defaulted to formatted instead of JSON | Force `--format json` |
255: | `Self-invocation refused` | The caller is already inside OpenCode (`OPENCODE_*` env, `opencode` ancestry or a state lock) | Use a different runtime, exit the current session or restate with explicit parallel-detached keywords |

257: | Context too large or truncated | The prompt references broad paths instead of specific files | Split large tasks and use `--file` for attachments |

260: 
261: ## 8. FAQ
262: 
263: **Q: What does the full-runtime dispatch buy over a sibling cli-* skill?**
264: 
265: A: A sibling cli-* skill dispatches to a single provider's binary. cli-opencode dispatches into a session that loads every plugin, skill and registered MCP server for the project. When the task needs a project-local skill, a project-specific plugin or the skill advisor, only cli-opencode provides all of them in one shot. When it only needs a model, a sibling is leaner.
266: 
267: **Q: When do I need a parallel detached session?**
268: 
269: A: When you are inside OpenCode and want a second session with its own state and session id. Common patterns are an ablation suite across sessions, a worker farm for parallel research and a cross-repo research branch. On OpenCode 2, `--port` has no `run` form (OpenCode 1 only). See [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md). The prompt must contain explicit parallel-session keywords or the self-invocation guard blocks the dispatch.
270: 
271: **Q: Why no top-level `--agent`?**
272: 
273: A: OpenCode 2 accepts `--agent general`. OpenCode 1 (fallback) treats named agents like `general` as subagents and will not run them at the top level: it prints a warning, falls back to the default agent and exits 0, so the flag does not select the requested agent. The default agent already covers the general case. For a specific profile, describe the role in the prompt body.
274: 
275: **Q: Why does a non-interactive dispatch hang without `</dev/null`?**
276: 
277: A: OpenCode reads stdin at startup before session creation. When stdout and stderr are redirected to files, stdin stays open and the process waits forever. Appending `</dev/null` provides an immediate EOF so the dispatch continues.
278: 
279: **Q: Which model do I pick?**
280: 
281: A: Default to `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` on both versions. On OpenCode 2 (the expected version) the default is `-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`, through the same gateway, because v2 lists no `opencode-go` provider unless it is logged in separately. On OpenCode 1 (fallback) that is `--model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max`, through the DevPass LLM Gateway, which fronts the latency-optimized reasoning model at its max thinking tier. The `opencode-go` Go-plan quota is spent, so that route hangs on "Go usage limit exceeded". One provider now serves both versions. Switch to `minimax/MiniMax-M3` for MiniMax Direct or `openai/gpt-6-sol` for paid premium. The full roster lives in `references/providers-and-models.md`.

# Skill README Template

Use this template for `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/README.md`. It writes a skill README in the same narrative voice the repo root `README.md` and the changelogs use: a one-line human pitch, an at-a-glance table near the top, a value-first overview, then quick start, navigation and a verification close.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

Give a person a fast, honest orientation to a skill before they open `SKILL.md`. The README answers what outcome the skill delivers, when to reach for it, what it does not own and how to navigate its files. `SKILL.md` stays the runtime instruction surface. The README is the front door a person reads.

### Identity Guidance (Purpose First)

The identity of a skill is the outcome it delivers. State that outcome in one plain sentence before naming tools.
Describe CLIs, commands, routing paths and reference files only after the outcome.
A README that opens with a tool name has not stated its identity.

The mcp-obsidian README states the outcome first: it makes AI use inside Obsidian effective.
It names the CLIs and MCP server later as delivery surfaces.
Repeat the outcome in the frontmatter description and the pitch.
The description supports a quick scan. The pitch opens the full README.

### Usage

Copy the fillable scaffold in Section 6 into `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/README.md`, then replace every placeholder with current behavior taken from the skill's real files. Keep the numbered ALL-CAPS section headers, the house style and the validator both require them. Drop any section that does not earn its place and renumber the rest.

### Template Focus

The README gives people a human entry point, current capabilities and a clear route to supporting files. This template provides:

- A one-line pitch in a blockquote right after the H1, stating the outcome before any tool name.
- An identity guidance block that puts the delivered outcome ahead of the tooling.
- A capability section pattern for a skill's headline strengths, modeled on the pilot's Plugin Knowledge Layer.
- A dedicated HVR enforcement section with the banned forms and the scripted checks.
- Versioning conventions and a validation checklist that matches the pilot's gates.

---

## 2. SECTION MODEL

A skill README uses numbered ALL-CAPS H2 sections with `---` dividers between them. The default order:

| # | Section | Purpose | Keep When |
|---|---------|---------|-----------|
| 1 | AT A GLANCE | Four-row table a reader scans in five seconds | Always |
| 2 | OVERVIEW | What the skill is and what the reader gets first, then the optional problem narrative | Always (required by the validator) |
| 3 | QUICK START | The fastest path to a first result | Skill has commands, scripts or a workflow |
| 4 | HOW IT WORKS | The main workflow in prose, with a small Mermaid diagram for multi-step flows | Skill has non-obvious behavior worth explaining |
| 5 | INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION | When to use it, plus how it hands off to sibling skills | Readers can confuse it with a neighbor |
| 6 | TROUBLESHOOTING | The failure modes operators actually hit | Predictable issues exist |
| 7 | FAQ | The two to five questions readers keep asking | High-value answers exist |
| 8 | VERIFICATION | How you know the skill works | Skill ships a playbook or validation command |
| 9 | RELATED DOCUMENTS | Stable links out, `SKILL.md` first | Always when links exist |

`OVERVIEW` is the one required section. Its normalized name must appear as a numbered header so the validator finds it. Every other section is optional. A small utility skill might run four sections (AT A GLANCE, OVERVIEW, QUICK START, RELATED DOCUMENTS). A large orchestrator might run all nine. Match the count to the skill. Never pad to hit a number.

Inside OVERVIEW, start with `### What It Does`. Say what the skill is and what the reader gets.
Add up to two optional subsections after it.
Use `### Why This Skill Exists` only to name a current reader problem.
Add the capability section below when it earns a table.

### Capability Section Pattern

When a skill has a headline strength, add a named capability section after What It Does.
Use one or two short sentences to say why the strength matters.
Use an analogy only when it clarifies the mechanism.
Name the section after its domain and add one table row per capability.
State the file or data the skill can operate on.
Avoid marketing claims. The prose explains why the capability matters. The table states what it does.

```markdown
### The Plugin Knowledge Layer

| Plugin | What the skill knows how to operate |
|---|---|
| **Beancount Ledger** | append and patch balanced transactions in the structured `.beancount` ledger |
| **Obsidian Tables** | edit `columns`, `rows` and `views` inside `.table.md` JSON payloads |
```

---

## 3. WRITING RULES

- Apply the [Prose Clarity Checklist](../../references/skill/creation-workflow.md#prose-clarity-checklist) to README prose.
- State the outcome before the tooling. The pitch and the identity guidance name what the reader gets. The tool names follow as the means.
- Open OVERVIEW with what the skill is and what the reader gets.
- Use `### Why This Skill Exists` only to explain a current reader problem.
- Add a short context hook after the blockquote only when it helps the reader. Keep AT A GLANCE as the first numbered section.
- Carry the explanation in prose. Reach for a table only when 4 or more parallel items need a lookup grid (skill relationships, CLI flags, a comparison).
- Use semantic emoji only (✅ ❌ ⚠️ 🔒 🚨) for rules and status markers. Decorative section emoji never: that register belongs to the repository front-page README, while a skill README keeps the technical formatting.
- A short, concrete analogy can carry an abstract mechanism better than adjectives (the repo root README uses "like a lab notebook for software"). Use one only where it clarifies, never as decoration.
- Put the AT A GLANCE table first. Four rows, one line each, no prose cells.
- Name the canonical command or entry point in OVERVIEW or QUICK START so a reader knows where to start.
- Link to real files under `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`, `feature-catalog/` or `manual-testing-playbook/`. Verify each path resolves.
- State the expected output for every command you show, so a reader can tell success from failure.
- Be honest about boundaries and trade-offs. If the skill does not own something, say which skill does.
- Keep `SKILL.md` as the runtime surface. The README explains why and how to navigate. It does not restate long reference files.
- Follow the Human Voice Rules. Section 4 lists the banned forms and the scripted checks. It links the full ruleset.
- Vary subsection counts rather than defaulting to three.
- Document current behavior. Keep spec history out of the README.
- Use stable paths and commands. Update the README, its version and its changelog entry when behavior changes.

---

The mcp-obsidian README states the outcome first: it makes AI use inside Obsidian effective.
It names the CLIs and MCP server later as delivery surfaces.
Repeat the outcome in the frontmatter description and the pitch.
The description supports a quick scan. The pitch opens the full README.

### Usage

Copy the fillable scaffold in Section 6 into `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/README.md`, then replace every placeholder with current behavior taken from the skill's real files. Keep the numbered ALL-CAPS section headers, the house style and the validator both require them. Drop any section that does not earn its place and renumber the rest.

### Template Focus

The README gives people a human entry point, current capabilities and a clear route to supporting files. This template provides:

- A one-line pitch in a blockquote right after the H1, stating the outcome before any tool name.
- An identity guidance block that puts the delivered outcome ahead of the tooling.
- A capability section pattern for a skill's headline strengths, modeled on the pilot's Plugin Knowledge Layer.
- A dedicated HVR enforcement section with the banned forms and the scripted checks.
- Versioning conventions and a validation checklist that matches the pilot's gates.

---

## 2. SECTION MODEL

A skill README uses numbered ALL-CAPS H2 sections with `---` dividers between them. The default order:

| # | Section | Purpose | Keep When |
|---|---------|---------|-----------|
| 1 | AT A GLANCE | Four-row table a reader scans in five seconds | Always |
| 2 | OVERVIEW | What the skill is and what the reader gets first, then the optional problem narrative | Always (required by the validator) |
| 3 | QUICK START | The fastest path to a first result | Skill has commands, scripts or a workflow |
| 4 | HOW IT WORKS | The main workflow in prose, with a small Mermaid diagram for multi-step flows | Skill has non-obvious behavior worth explaining |
| 5 | INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION | When to use it, plus how it hands off to sibling skills | Readers can confuse it with a neighbor |
| 6 | TROUBLESHOOTING | The failure modes operators actually hit | Predictable issues exist |
| 7 | FAQ | The two to five questions readers keep asking | High-value answers exist |
| 8 | VERIFICATION | How you know the skill works | Skill ships a playbook or validation command |
| 9 | RELATED DOCUMENTS | Stable links out, `SKILL.md` first | Always when links exist |

`OVERVIEW` is the one required section. Its normalized name must appear as a numbered header so the validator finds it. Every other section is optional. A small utility skill might run four sections (AT A GLANCE, OVERVIEW, QUICK START, RELATED DOCUMENTS). A large orchestrator might run all nine. Match the count to the skill. Never pad to hit a number.

Inside OVERVIEW, start with `### What It Does`. Say what the skill is and what the reader gets.
Add up to two optional subsections after it.
Use `### Why This Skill Exists` only to name a current reader problem.
Add the capability section below when it earns a table.

### Capability Section Pattern

When a skill has a headline strength, add a named capability section after What It Does.
Use one or two short sentences to say why the strength matters.
Use an analogy only when it clarifies the mechanism.
Name the section after its domain and add one table row per capability.
State the file or data the skill can operate on.
Avoid marketing claims. The prose explains why the capability matters. The table states what it does.

```markdown
### The Plugin Knowledge Layer

| Plugin | What the skill knows how to operate |
|---|---|
| **Beancount Ledger** | append and patch balanced transactions in the structured `.beancount` ledger |
| **Obsidian Tables** | edit `columns`, `rows` and `views` inside `.table.md` JSON payloads |
```

---

## 3. WRITING RULES

- Apply the [Prose Clarity Checklist](../../references/skill/creation-workflow.md#prose-clarity-checklist) to README prose.
- State the outcome before the tooling. The pitch and the identity guidance name what the reader gets. The tool names follow as the means.
- Open OVERVIEW with what the skill is and what the reader gets.
- Use `### Why This Skill Exists` only to explain a current reader problem.
- Add a short context hook after the blockquote only when it helps the reader. Keep AT A GLANCE as the first numbered section.
- Carry the explanation in prose. Reach for a table only when 4 or more parallel items need a lookup grid (skill relationships, CLI flags, a comparison).
- Use semantic emoji only (✅ ❌ ⚠️ 🔒 🚨) for rules and status markers. Decorative section emoji never: that register belongs to the repository front-page README, while a skill README keeps the technical formatting.
- A short, concrete analogy can carry an abstract mechanism better than adjectives (the repo root README uses "like a lab notebook for software"). Use one only where it clarifies, never as decoration.
- Put the AT A GLANCE table first. Four rows, one line each, no prose cells.
- Name the canonical command or entry point in OVERVIEW or QUICK START so a reader knows where to start.
- Link to real files under `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`, `feature-catalog/` or `manual-testing-playbook/`. Verify each path resolves.
- State the expected output for every command you show, so a reader can tell success from failure.
- Be honest about boundaries and trade-offs. If the skill does not own something, say which skill does.
- Keep `SKILL.md` as the runtime surface. The README explains why and how to navigate. It does not restate long reference files.
- Follow the Human Voice Rules. Section 4 lists the banned forms and the scripted checks. It links the full ruleset.
- Vary subsection counts rather than defaulting to three.
- Document current behavior. Keep spec history out of the README.
- Use stable paths and commands. Update the README, its version and its changelog entry when behavior changes.

---

## 4. HVR ENFORCEMENT

174: - Refuse ambiguous self-invocation.
175: - Run provider pre-flight for model/auth errors.
176: - Check version drift for unknown flags.
177: - Force `--format json` for empty streams.
178: - Add `</dev/null` for background loops.
179: - Never pass `--share`.
180: - Use `--pure` only for plugin crashes; it is absent from OpenCode 2 `run` and available on OpenCode 1 only (see [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md)).
181: - Inspect state logs for stuck sessions.
182: 
183: ---
184: 
185: ## 4. RULES
186: 
187: ### ✅ ALWAYS
188: 
189: 1. Verify OpenCode CLI is installed before first invocation. Confirm the version baseline for OpenCode 2 (2.1.4, the expected version) or OpenCode 1 (1.19.4, supported for now as a fallback), with drift handling per `references/cli-reference.md` §9.
190: 2. **Run the self-invocation guard before dispatch** (ADR-001): Layer 1 env-var lookup for any `OPENCODE_*`, Layer 2 process-ancestry probe for `opencode` parent, Layer 3 `~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock` probe. Trip on ANY positive. Refuse unless the prompt has explicit parallel-session keywords.
191: 3. Pin model, variant, format and dir explicitly.
192:    - OpenCode 2 default: `-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json` with a start-in-directory `cd`.
193:    - OpenCode 1 fallback: `--model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --variant max --format json --dir <repo-root>` (see [`references/cli-reference.md`](./references/cli-reference.md) §4).
194:    - **No `--agent`**: the Default Invocation note says top-level `--agent general` is rejected. Put agent-profile requests in the prompt body.
195:    - Honor user overrides verbatim. Check the id against the roster in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md) rather than memory; each provider allows a specific set and a specific id shape.
196: 4. Pass `--format json` unless the calling AI explicitly wants formatted output. The JSON event stream is what external runtimes parse incrementally.
197: 5. **Append `</dev/null` to every non-interactive `opencode run` invocation** when it redirects stdout and/or stderr to files or runs inside `while read` loops.
198:    - Without a closed stdin, `opencode run` hangs at 0% CPU.
199:    - Place it after the prompt positional argument and before the `> stdout 2> stderr` redirects.
200:    - **DO NOT auto-kill external operator-owned opencode sessions** when sweeping orphans. Exclude `opencode run` from pkill.
201:    - Hang mechanics and failure patterns: [`references/integration-patterns.md`](./references/integration-patterns.md) §6.
202: 6. **Pass the spec folder to the dispatched session** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating: the dispatched session cannot answer Gate 3 interactively in non-interactive `run` mode.
203: 7. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 2-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:
204:    1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card. Framework selection uses the canonical card's cross-model defaults, with no per-model prompt-craft profiles.
205:    2. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 2** trigger applies. The Tier 2 trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`. Do not re-enumerate it here.
206: 8. Validate dispatched session output: parse JSON events incrementally (tool calls, partial messages, final summary), run syntax checks if code generated, and cross-reference against project standards via `sk-code` surface detection plus its code-review mode for findings-first review (see ALWAYS rule 12).
207: 9. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) to catch tool errors and warnings.
208: 10. Classify the use case (1 / 2 / 3) before dispatching. The smart router refuses dispatches that do not map to one of the three.
209: 11. **Run the Provider Auth Pre-Flight once per session** (see §3 Provider Auth Pre-Flight). Cache the configured-providers list. If the default provider is missing (`llmgateway` on both versions), ASK the user. Never silently substitute the model. If a later dispatch returns an auth error, invalidate the cache and rerun the pre-flight before retrying.
210: 12. **Code Standards Loading (surface-aware contract):** For code review or generation, instruct the session to:
211:     - (1) Load `sk-code`.
212:     - (2) Let `sk-code` emit a surface tag matching the detected stack.
213:     - (3) Load selected surface resources and run its verification commands.
214:     - (4) Load `sk-code`'s code-review mode only for formal findings-first review output.
215:     - If the surface cannot be determined confidently, ask for the runtime surface and verification command set.
216:     - NEVER hardcode obsolete sibling code skills in dispatch prompts.
217: 13. **Design Standards Loading (measured-reference contract):** For design or UI work, instruct the session to:
218:    - (1) Load `sk-design-md-generator`.
219:    - (2) Extract a measured Style Reference DESIGN.md (named color tokens, type scale, components, Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind) from the live source before building UI.
220:    - (3) Build against those measured tokens and run the extraction's validate step to confirm hex/section fidelity.
221:    - If no live source can be measured, ask for the reference URL or exact tokens.
222:    - NEVER treat `mcp-figma` or `sk-design-md-generator` as a taste or critique authority. The extraction measures real CSS; it does not judge design.
223: 14. **Pass the design reference manifest to the dispatched session:** For design or UI work, inline a `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST v1` block in the prompt.
224:     - The child cannot resolve skill paths; the manifest must travel in the payload, not by reference.
225:     - Include `styleReferenceExtracted` true, the measured live `source`, measured design tokens / type scale / components, `loadedFiles` and `proofDemandBack`.
226:     - If you lack a Style Reference or a live source, ask before launching; do not start a silent dispatch.
227:     - The child returns the demanded proof. The parent reconciles it on return.
228: 15. **Destructive-scope-violation prevention (RM-8) for deep-loop dispatches.**
229:     - The permissions-matrix gate (`permissions-gate.ts`) has no production caller. A `--permissions-matrix <path>` config is not enforced and bypasses nothing (wiring status: `references/permissions-matrix.md`).
230:     - For non-interactive `opencode run` with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` against a populated worktree, you MUST apply the four-layer mitigation, the only active protection:
231:       - (L1) The rendered prompt contains literal `BANNED OPERATIONS` and `ALLOWED WRITE PATHS`.
232:       - (L2) The working directory points to a fresh `git worktree` (OpenCode 2: start-in-directory `cd`; OpenCode 1: `--dir <path>`).
233:       - (L3) Commit the target's own in-flight changes by explicit path. Leave other sessions' changes alone and record the recovery-baseline commit hash.
234:       - (L4) For multi-phase / phase-parent targets, prefer `cli-copilot` + `gpt-6-sol --reasoning-effort high` over the DeepSeek V4 Flash default, after confirming that model on the Copilot surface.
235:     - The 2026-05-04 incident deleted 44 files. See `references/destructive-scope-violations.md` for its root cause and checklist.
236: 16. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).**
237:     - Launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time. Wait for it to return and verify its outputs.
238:     - Then SIGKILL only the dispatch this skill started, using its captured PID and that PID's own children. Never use a blanket `pkill -9 -f "opencode run"` (see Rule 5).
239:     - Deep-flow sessions chain iterations back-to-back with kill-between. Explicitly authorized parallel dispatches are each killed by their own PID.
240:     - Full procedure: [`references/integration-patterns.md`](./references/integration-patterns.md) §8.
241: 17. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched session's env AND state the exemption in the prompt.**
242:     - A model cannot see an environment variable. Given only the variable, a session still asks the documentation-scope question and writes nothing at exit code zero.
243:     - Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt.
244:     - The variable also tells the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`) that dispatched `opencode run` is an orchestrated sub-session sharing the parent's worktree rather than allocating its own.
245:     - The wrapper checks `AI_SESSION_CHILD` plus a `git --git-common-dir` backstop, then execs in place when set.
246:     - Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode run ... </dev/null`. Harmless when the wrapper is not in use.
247:     - See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → "Worktree session isolation".
248:     - Prepend `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0` next to it so the child never inherits an enforced spec-gate from the parent shell: `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode run ... </dev/null`.
249: 
250: 18. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).** Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}`, never a bare task.
251:     - Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9 (`.opencode/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, etc.). Never hardcode one runtime.
252:     - Map each subtask to the RIGHT agent, not one default: `code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, docs→`markdown`.
253:     - **OpenCode reaches personas via a primary:** route `--agent orchestrate` (or another primary) so the resolved persona runs as a Task subagent. Top-level `--agent` rejects `mode: subagent` personas (see [`references/agent-delegation.md`](./references/agent-delegation.md)).
254:     - On a bare `opencode run` that names no subagent, **INLINE** the persona block into the payload using the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 14); the child cannot resolve agent paths by reference.
255:     - A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant, silently dropping its tool-scope, verification gates and output contract.
256:     - Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection". Native precedent: `orchestrate.md` "Agent Loading Protocol".
257:     - Declare rare exceptions at the dispatch site: native surface used, focused summary for a small-context model, or pure-mechanical command.
258: 
259: ### ⛔ NEVER
260: 
261: 1. Invoke this skill from within OpenCode itself for a self-dispatch. Refuse with the documented error message and use a sibling cli-* / fresh shell / parallel-session keywords.
262: 2. Pass `--share`. OpenCode 2 `run` has no such flag, and on OpenCode 1.19.3 (fallback) it is a hidden, deprecated flag that only prints "Session sharing has been discontinued" (see [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md)).
263: 3. Trust dispatched session output blindly for security-sensitive code, send sensitive data (API keys, passwords, credentials) in prompts, or hammer the API with rapid sequential calls.
264: 4. Use `--pure` outside of plugin debugging (absent from OpenCode 2 `run`, OpenCode 1 only, see [`references/install-and-versions.md`](./references/install-and-versions.md)). Disabling plugins removes the entire point of cli-opencode dispatch.
265: 5. Nest `opencode run` inside a dispatched session's tool calls. Use OpenCode's native Task tool for sub-agent dispatch.
266: 
267: ### ⚠️ ESCALATE IF
268: 
269: 1. OpenCode CLI is not installed and user has not acknowledged (provide `brew install opencode` or `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`).
270: 2. Operator asks for a share URL. OpenCode 2 `run` has no share flag, and OpenCode 1.19.3 discontinued session sharing, so say there is no URL to publish.
271: 3. Binary version differs from the OpenCode 2 (2.1.4, expected) or OpenCode 1 (1.19.4, fallback) baseline. Run `opencode --version` (`opencode1 --version` for the side-by-side OpenCode 1) and `run --help`, then surface drift and fall back or require approval.
272: 4. Smart router cannot map the prompt to one of the three use cases. Surface the disambiguation checklist from UNKNOWN_FALLBACK.
273: 5. Self-invocation guard trips AND the prompt is ambiguous. Surface the refusal with three remediation options (sibling cli-* / fresh shell / parallel-session keywords).
274: 
275: ### Memory Handback Protocol
276: 
277: When you need to preserve session context from an OpenCode CLI delegation, run the canonical procedure: extract `MEMORY_HANDBACK`, scrub secrets, and invoke `generate-context.js` via `--stdin`/`--json`/temp-file.

281:

286: printf '%s' "$JSON_PAYLOAD" | node .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js --stdin [spec-folder]
287: ```

2: name: cli-opencode
